results.summary: The bounded search found the current council-run Arts on Estates programme. It is absent from the catalogue and candidate history, and the council page establishes the activity, intended residents, mostly-free status and public route for finding current sessions.

resource.name: Arts on Estates — Islington creative activities
resource.description: Creative activities including art, singing, crafts, knitting, pottery and printmaking through community centres, hubs and partner venues.
resource.who: Islington council estate residents who find mainstream arts difficult to access because of financial, health or social barriers.
resource.access: Email partnerships@islington.gov.uk to join the Community Partnerships mailing list and ask about upcoming activities.
resource.check: The programme is mostly free and activities change with demand. Confirm the current activity, venue, eligibility, accessibility and any charge before attending.
resource.coverage: Islington council estates, through local community centres, hubs and partner venues.

sources.note: The council page describes the estate-resident audience, examples of creative activities, mostly-free status, delivery settings and mailing-list contact.

candidates.evidence: Islington Council describes an ongoing creative programme for estate residents facing barriers to mainstream arts and publishes a direct email route for current opportunities.
candidates.limitations: The page does not publish a current timetable, individual venues, age rules for every activity, accessibility details or which activities carry a charge.

results.summary: The bounded search found Islington Chinese Association absent from the catalogue and history. Its current provider site and NHS profile establish cultural and social activities, an Islington base, an open audience and self-referral/contact routes.

resource.name: Islington Chinese Association — culture and community
resource.description: Chinese cultural, recreational and social activities that help people connect, share traditions and build community.
resource.who: People of all races and age groups who want to connect with the community or learn about Chinese culture.
resource.access: Use the provider website's membership link, email info@islingtonchinese.com or call 020 7263 5986 to ask about current activities. The NHS profile says people can self-refer.
resource.check: Ask about the current activity timetable, membership arrangements, availability, accessibility and any charges before visiting.
resource.coverage: Based in Islington; the NHS profile lists the London Borough of Islington and neighbouring boroughs.

sources.note: The current provider site describes its social-cohesion purpose, Chinese cultural and community activities, open welcome, membership route and active November 2026 updates.
The NHS profile confirms the address, phone, email, Islington and neighbouring-borough catchment, open audience, self-referral and wheelchair access.

candidates.evidence: Current provider and NHS pages establish an active Islington community organisation offering Chinese cultural and social connection, with public membership and self-referral contact routes.
candidates.limitations: The pages do not establish the current timetable, availability or membership and activity charges. Individual activities may have different access requirements.

resource.name: Society of Fulham Artists and Potters
resource.description: A local art society offering exhibitions, tutor-led workshops, plein-air days, talks, social events and connections with other artists.
resource.who: People aged 18 or over who live, work or study in Hammersmith and Fulham or a neighbouring borough.
resource.access: Complete the provider's online joining form or email members@sofap.co.uk to ask about membership.
resource.check: Annual membership is listed as £45. Members are expected to help at events they take part in; confirm the current fee, workshop charges, dates and accessibility before joining.
resource.sourceOwner: Society of Fulham Artists and Potters
resource.coverage: Hammersmith and Fulham and neighbouring boroughs.

sources.note: The current provider homepage confirms the society's local purpose, adult area criteria, events, workshops and public membership route.

candidates.evidence: Current provider pages establish an active local adult art society with a direct joining route and a clear programme of creative and social opportunities.
candidates.limitations: The pages do not establish accessibility, capacity or the cost and schedule of each workshop or event. Membership is not free and includes a volunteering expectation.

resource.name: HF Mencap — My Life Day Opportunities
resource.description: Tailored day support and activity-centre sessions for adults with learning disabilities, autism or complex needs, including social, creative, fitness and independence activities.
resource.who: Adults aged 18 or over with learning disabilities, autism or complex support needs.
resource.access: Contact HF Mencap to arrange a visit and support assessment. A package can be funded by a local authority or arranged using a Direct Payment.
resource.check: Centre activities are free to My Life clients; some external activities have a small charge. Confirm funding, assessment, schedule, transport, current availability and any activity costs.
resource.coverage: Activity hubs in Hammersmith and Fulham; the provider says it supports clients across Central and West London boroughs.

sources.note: The current service page confirms the adult audience, activities, funding routes, assessment, locations, phone, client costs and wider Central and West London reach.
The provider overview confirms My Life as a current HF Mencap support and activity-centre service for people with learning disabilities.

candidates.evidence: HF Mencap's current pages describe a distinct adult day-opportunity service, its activities, access assessment, funding arrangements and two Hammersmith and Fulham hubs.
candidates.limitations: A support assessment and funding arrangement are required. The pages do not establish current capacity, waiting times, individual accessibility needs or the exact cost of external activities.
